entities.name: Heteroaryl bromide substrate
observations: Tokenized structure decodes approximately as CCCN1N=C2C=CC(Br)=CC2=C1C.
Contains an aryl or heteroaryl C–Br bond available for substitution.

entities.name: NH pyridone substrate
observations: Tokenized structure decodes approximately as O=C1C=C(OCC2=CC=C(Cl)C=C2)C=C[NH]1.
Contains an NH-containing pyridone or lactam nitrogen and a retained carbonyl.

entities.name: Heteroaryl N-arylation
observations: The product is consistent with replacing the heteroaryl C–Br bond by a C–N bond to the pyridone nitrogen.
The lactam carbonyl is retained, supporting N-arylation rather than carbonyl transformation or ring annulation.

entities.name: Buchwald-Hartwig conditions
observations: Plausible catalyst systems include Pd2(dba)3 or Pd(OAc)2 with Xantphos, BINAP, BrettPhos, RuPhos, or DavePhos.
Plausible bases include Cs2CO3, K3PO4, NaOtBu, or KOtBu; plausible solvents include 1,4-dioxane, toluene, DMF, NMP, or tert-amyl alcohol; typical temperature is about 80–120 °C.

entities.name: Ullmann N-arylation conditions
observations: A secondary possibility is CuI or Cu2O with 1,10-phenanthroline or related ligand, Cs2CO3 or K2CO3, and DMF or DMSO at roughly 90–120 °C.

entities.name: Direct SNAr conditions
observations: Direct displacement is possible if the heteroaryl bromide is sufficiently electron deficient, using K2CO3, Cs2CO3, or DIPEA in DMF, DMSO, or NMP with heating.
